summary: Exception tags can cause host data structures to be unaligned
description:
Wasmtime's internal `VMContext` data structure lays out its contents to match a particular input WebAssembly module and maps the module's own constructs to host data structures. A bug in this logic meant that when a module contained an odd number of tags then future internal fields were mis-aligned. A mis-aligned host structure is undefined behavior in Rust.

## Impact

There is no known way at this time this issue can be exploited. Nevertheless mis-aligned data structures are undefined behavior in Rust and can become more serious bugs as revisions of the Rust compiler and LLVM are released, for example. This advisory is being issued to notify that users should update to a patched release of Wasmtime where this undefined behavior is not present.

This advisory only affects embedders that have WebAssembly exceptions enabled, and exceptions are enabled by default in Wasmtime 47.0.0 and later.

## Patches

The fix is present in main and patch releases are made for 48.0.6 and 49.0.3.

## Workarounds

Disable exception support in the CLI via `-W exceptions=n` or the API via `Config::wasm_exceptions(false)`.
